newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends flat, dollar build-ups seen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends flat, dollar build-ups seen.

text.p: The won closed flat against the dollar on Thursday after a day of tight-range trading, but sentiment for the dollar is expected to strengthen on Friday due to more importer settlements, brokers said.
"Trading was thin in the absence of fresh factors. But the dollar is likely to strengthen tomorrow due to import deals," said Kim Ki-baek, a dealer at the Korea Exchange Bank .
The won closed at the opening level of 827.70. It ranged from 827.50 to 828.30.
Dealers said the dollar's rise against the yen was expected to put downward pressure on the won.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 828.00 on Friday, compared with 826.90 today.
Dealers said the won was currently under pressure due to strong dollar demand for importer settlements.
"We will see the dollar rise throughout next week," Kim said. He forecast trading would move between 827.00 and 829.50 on Friday.
Kim Jin-kyu of Citibank predicted a range of 826.80 to 828.50.
